name: Path Dimension
definition: The **path dimension** $\mathrm P(\mathcal H)$ is the largest $d$ for which some $S=\{x_1,\ldots,x_d\}\subseteq\mathcal X$ and $T\subseteq S$ satisfy $$T\mathbin{\triangle}\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}\in\mathcal H_{|S}\quad\text{for every }0\leq k\leq d.$$ Thus $\mathcal H_{|S}$ contains a path through all $d+1$ successive traces.
graph_summary: The maximum length of a one-coordinate-at-a-time path through the class.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: A path witness contained in a subfamily remains contained in the larger class.

p_monotonic.proof: A path witness in a projection is already realized by the original class on those coordinates.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Counterexample to strict c-monotonicity: for $\mathcal H=\{0000,0001,0010,0011,0100,0111,1001,1010\}$, conditioning the third coordinate gives two fibres of path dimension 3, while $\mathrm P(\mathcal H)=3$.
